category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Identify the primary organ of steroid catabolism and the two biochemical modifications required to prepare testosterone for urinary excretion.
back:
• Organ: Liver
• Modifications: Reduction of unsaturated bonds (hydrogenation) and conjugation with glucuronic acid or sulfate
• Result: Increased water solubility for excretion

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: In the systemic circulation, the majority of testosterone and estradiol is transported bound to [___], while a smaller, non-specific fraction is bound to albumin.
back:
• Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG)
• Only the 'free' (unbound) steroid fraction is biologically active
• Liver disease can alter transport by decreasing SHBG synthesis

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A 30-year-old female is in her third trimester of pregnancy. Which estrogen isomer is predominantly produced by the syncytiotrophoblast using fetal precursors, and what is its relative potency compared to estradiol?
back:
• Estriol (E3)
• Produced from fetal 16-OH-DHEA-S
• Least potent estrogen; serves as a marker of fetal-placental well-being

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Explain the role of the Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory (StAR) protein in the biosynthesis of testosterone within Leydig cells.
back:
• Transports cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane
• This is the essential regulated step for providing substrate to P450scc
• Stimulated by LH via the cAMP/PKA pathway

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the physiological role of Luteinizing Hormone (LH) in males versus females regarding sex steroid regulation.
back:
• Males: Stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone.
• Females: Triggers ovulation and stimulates the corpus luteum to secrete progesterone and estrogen.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Name the 17-ketosteroid metabolic products of testosterone found in the urine and the primary strong androgen formed in peripheral tissues like the prostate.
back:
• Urinary products: Androsterone and Etiocholanolone
• Peripheral strong androgen: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT)
• DHT formation: Catalyzed by 5-alpha-reductase

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: In the biosynthesis of estrogens from androgens, the enzyme responsible for the aromatization of the A-ring is [___].
back:
• Aromatase (CYP19)
• Converts testosterone to estradiol
• Converts androstenedione to estrone in peripheral tissues
• Crucial for female secondary sex characteristics.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A 24-year-old female presents with hirsutism, acne, and irregular menstrual cycles. Labs show elevated testosterone levels. Identify the primary ovarian cell type responsible for excess androgen production in this patient.
back:
• Theca cells
• Stimulated by Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
• Provide androstenedione and testosterone precursors for granulosa cells via the 2-cell theory.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Explain the biochemical transport mechanism of testosterone and estrogen in the plasma.
back:
• Primarily bound to Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG)
• Non-specifically bound to Albumin
• Only the free (unbound) fraction is biologically active and can diffuse into target cells.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the primary site of testosterone synthesis in males with the primary site of estradiol synthesis in females.
back:
• Testosterone: Leydig cells of the testes (LH stimulation)
• Estradiol: Granulosa cells of the ovarian follicles (FSH stimulation of aromatase)
• Both utilize cholesterol as the initial precursor.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Describe the primary pathway for the catabolism and excretion of steroid sex hormones.
back:
• Occurs primarily in the liver
• Includes reduction of unsaturated bonds and hydroxylation
• Conjugation with glucuronic acid or sulfate ensures water solubility for urinary or fecal excretion.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: The conversion of cholesterol to [___] by the enzyme desmolase (P450scc) is the shared rate-limiting step for the synthesis of testosterone, progesterone, and estrogen.
back:
• Pregnenolone
• Occurs in the inner mitochondrial membrane
• Regulated by the Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory (StAR) protein transport mechanism.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman with estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer is prescribed an aromatase inhibitor. Identify the primary tissue source of estrogen in this patient.
back:
• Peripheral adipose tissue
• Site of conversion of adrenal androgens (androstenedione) into estrone
• Aromatase inhibitors block this extra-gonadal estrogen production.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Describe the biochemical mechanism of action of progesterone on its target cells.
back:
• Diffuses across plasma membrane to bind nuclear receptors
• Receptor-ligand complex dimerizes and binds to Progesterone Response Elements (PRE) on DNA
• Directly regulates gene transcription and protein synthesis.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Distinguish between Testosterone and Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) regarding their synthesis and potency.
back:
• DHT is synthesized from testosterone by 5α-reductase
• DHT has a much higher affinity for the androgen receptor
• Essential for male external genitalia and prostate development.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Identify the essential biochemical role of progesterone during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle.
back:
• Maintains secretory endometrium for possible implantation
• Exerts negative feedback on LH and FSH secretion
• Increases basal body temperature (thermogenic effect).

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: In the biosynthesis of steroid hormones, the rate-limiting conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
• Desmolase (CYP11A1 / Cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme).
• Requires NADPH and O2.
• Occurs in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A postmenopausal female with estrogen-responsive breast cancer is treated with an inhibitor to block the peripheral conversion of androstenedione to estrogen. This drug targets the enzyme [___].
back:
• Aromatase (CYP19).
• Role: Converts androgens (testosterone/androstenedione) into estrogens.
• Major source of estrogen in postmenopausal women (adipose tissue).

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Explain the general mechanism of action for steroid hormones like testosterone and estrogen once they reach their target cell.
back:
• Diffusion: Cross plasma membrane (lipophilic).
• Binding: Interact with specific cytosolic or nuclear receptors.
• Transcription: Receptor-ligand dimers bind DNA Hormone Response Elements (HREs) to regulate gene expression.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the biochemical roles and potencies of Testosterone versus Dihydrotestosterone (DHT).
back:
• Testosterone: Influences internal genitalia (Wolffian ducts) and skeletal muscle.
• DHT: More potent metabolite formed via 5-alpha-reductase; influences external genitalia and prostate.
• Receptor: Both bind the same androgen receptor, but DHT has higher affinity.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Identify the pituitary hormone that stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone and specify the intracellular second messenger involved.
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH).
• Second Messenger: cAMP.
• Effect: Activates PKA, which phosphorylates StAR protein to facilitate cholesterol transport.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: The primary plasma protein responsible for transporting the majority of circulating testosterone and estradiol in the blood is [___].
back:
• Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG).
• Albumin: Acts as a non-specific, low-affinity carrier.
• Activity: Only the 'free' (unbound) hormone fraction is biologically active.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
coreConcept: Progesterone Synthesis and Role in Pregnancy
front: A woman in early pregnancy has insufficient hormonal support for the uterine lining. This required hormone is primarily secreted by the [___] during the first trimester.
back:
• Progesterone.
• Source: Corpus Luteum (until placental takeover).
• Role: Maintains the secretory endometrium for pregnancy survival.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Describe the biochemical modifications occurring in the liver to facilitate the catabolism and excretion of steroid hormones.
back:
• Reduction: Saturation of double bonds and addition of hydroxyl groups.
• Conjugation: Attachment to glucuronic acid or sulfate.
• Result: Increases water solubility for excretion in urine or bile.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Distinguish between Estradiol (E2) and Estrone (E1) regarding their primary physiological source and relative potency.
back:
• Estradiol (E2): Ovarian origin; predominant in premenopausal women; most potent estrogen.
• Estrone (E1): Adipose origin; predominant in postmenopausal women; lower potency.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Name the 21-carbon steroid that serves as the immediate common precursor ('parent compound') for all classes of steroid hormones.
back:
• Pregnenolone.
• Biosynthesis: Derived from 27-carbon Cholesterol.
• Fate: Converted to Progesterone or 17-hydroxypregnenolone.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: ACTH is synthesized as part of a large, multi-domain precursor molecule known as [___].
back: * Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC); * Large polypeptide containing sequences for ACTH, MSH, and endorphins; * Undergoes tissue-specific proteolytic cleavage.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: A patient with primary adrenal insufficiency presents with darkened skin creases and buccal mucosa. This hyperpigmentation occurs because high ACTH cross-reacts with [___] receptors.
back: * Melanocortin-1 (MC1R) receptors; * ACTH shares a core amino acid sequence with MSH; * Direct stimulation of melanocytes increases melanin production.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Explain how the pituitary produces both ACTH and beta-endorphin from a single gene product.
back: * Translated as a single POMC pro-hormone; * Subject to post-translational cleavage by Proprotein Convertases (PC1/PC2); * Specific fragments are released based on enzyme expression.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Contrast the POMC cleavage products formed in the anterior pituitary with those formed in the intermediate lobe.
back: * Anterior: Produces ACTH and beta-lipotropin; * Intermediate: Further processes ACTH into alpha-MSH; * Intermediate: Cleaves beta-lipotropin into gamma-LPH and beta-endorphin.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: State the biological significance of the shared amino acid sequence between ACTH and the various isomers of MSH.
back: * Common heptapeptide 'core' sequence; * Allows high levels of ACTH to bind MC1R; * Explains cutaneous signs in ACTH-secreting tumors.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: The molecule [___] is a fragment of the POMC precursor that acts as the direct parent molecule for both gamma-lipotropin and beta-endorphin.
back: * Beta-lipotropin (beta-LPH); * Secreted in equimolar amounts with ACTH; * Contains the sequence for endogenous opioid peptides.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: A patient develops Nelson syndrome (intense hyperpigmentation) after bilateral adrenalectomy. Relate the hormone excess to the observed physical sign.
back: * Loss of cortisol negative feedback; * Massive upregulation of POMC gene transcription; * Excess ACTH and MSH fragments stimulate skin melanocytes.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Describe the specific intracellular signaling pathway utilized by CRH to induce the synthesis and secretion of ACTH peptides.
back: * CRH binds GPCR on corticotrophs; * Activates Adenylyl Cyclase and increases cAMP; * PKA triggers POMC gene transcription and vesicle release.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Distinguish between the derivation of alpha-MSH and beta-MSH within the pituitary processing pathway.
back: * Alpha-MSH: Derived from the N-terminal cleavage of ACTH; * Beta-MSH: Contained within the gamma-lipotropin fragment; * Both promote melanogenesis via receptor cross-reactivity.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Identify the specific family of endoproteases responsible for the site-specific hydrolytic cleavage of the inactive POMC pro-hormone.
back: * Proprotein Convertases (PC); * Specifically PC1 (or PC3) and PC2; * Serine proteases that recognize dibasic amino acid motifs.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: The primary enzyme responsible for the conversion of testosterone into estradiol within the ovaries and peripheral adipose tissue is [___].
back:
• Aromatase (CYP19).
• A cytochrome P450 monooxygenase.
• Targeted by inhibitors in postmenopausal estrogen-responsive breast cancer.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A 16-year-old phenotypic female presents with primary amenorrhea. Karyotype is 46,XY. Lab results show high serum testosterone levels. The failure of male sexual differentiation in this patient is due to a defect in [___].
back:
• Androgen Receptor (AR).
• Condition: Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome.
• Results in failure of the hormone-receptor complex to bind DNA response elements.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Explain the role of the zinc finger motif within the mechanism of action of steroid hormones like progesterone.
back:
• Located in the DNA-binding domain of the receptor.
• Mediates binding of the hormone-receptor complex to specific DNA sequences (HREs).
• Facilitates the dimerization required for transcriptional regulation.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the effects of 21-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency versus 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency on sex hormone levels and clinical presentation.
back:
• 21-hydroxylase: Shunts precursors to androgens; causes virilization/ambiguous genitalia.
• 17-hydroxylase: Blocks androgen/estrogen synthesis; causes primary amenorrhea and female phenotype (regardless of genotype).

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Specify the rate-limiting step and the specific mitochondrial enzyme involved in the biosynthesis of all steroid hormones from cholesterol.
back:
• Conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone.
• Enzyme: Side-chain cleavage enzyme (P450scc / Desmolase).
• Requires NADPH and molecular oxygen.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: In the systemic circulation, roughly 98% of testosterone and estradiol are transported bound to [___].
back:
• Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG).
• Albumin (acts as a non-specific, lower-affinity carrier).
• Only the 'free' fraction is biologically active.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A patient with liver cirrhosis shows signs of 'feminization,' including gynecomastia. This occurs because the liver is unable to perform its role in [___].
back:
• Catabolism and excretion of estrogens.
• Estrogens are normally conjugated with glucuronic acid or sulfate in the liver.
• Impaired clearance leads to accumulation in the blood.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Describe the biochemical sequence by which Luteinizing Hormone (LH) initiates testosterone production in testicular Leydig cells.
back:
• LH binds GPCR, activating adenylyl cyclase.
• Increased cAMP activates Protein Kinase A (PKA).
• PKA stimulates StAR protein to transport cholesterol to the inner mitochondrial membrane.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the primary sources of progesterone production during the first trimester of pregnancy versus the subsequent trimesters.
back:
• 1st Trimester: Corpus luteum (maintained by hCG).
• 2nd/3rd Trimesters: Placenta (converts maternal cholesterol to progesterone independently).

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Identify the parent steroid compound from which all androgens, estrogens, and glucocorticoids are derived after cholesterol cleavage.
back:
• Pregnenolone.
• Formed in the mitochondria.
• Serves as the universal precursor for steroidogenesis.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: The rate-limiting enzyme that converts cholesterol into pregnenolone during the biosynthesis of all sex steroids is [___].
back:
**Cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme (P450scc/Desmolase)**

- Located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
- Requires NADPH and molecular oxygen.
- Mediated by StAR protein which moves cholesterol into the mitochondria.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A 60-year-old female with breast cancer is treated with an inhibitor of Aromatase (CYP19). This drug directly prevents the conversion of [___] to [___].
back:
**Androgens (Testosterone/Androstenedione) to Estrogens**

- Aromatase catalyzes the aromatization of the steroid A-ring.
- Crucial for postmenopausal estrogen production in peripheral adipose tissue.
- Inhibitors reduce growth signaling in estrogen-dependent tumors.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Explain the specific role of the Zinc finger motif in the mechanism of action of testosterone and estrogen.
back:
**DNA-Binding Domain Interaction**

- Hormone-receptor complexes dimerize and enter the nucleus.
- Zinc fingers recognize and bind specific **Hormone Response Elements (HREs)** on DNA.
- This binding recruits coactivators to initiate mRNA transcription of target genes.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the blood transport mechanisms of active gonadal steroids with their hepatic catabolic metabolites.
back:
**Protein-Bound vs. Free (Conjugated)**

- **Active Steroids:** Bound tightly to **Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG)** or albumin.
- **Metabolites:** Liver conjugates them with **glucuronic acid or sulfate**.
- Conjugation increases water solubility, allowing free transport and renal excretion.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Detail the biochemical steps involved in the regulation of testosterone secretion by Luteinizing Hormone (LH) in Leydig cells.
back:
**LH-cAMP-StAR Pathway**

- LH binds GPCR, increasing intracellular **cAMP**.
- Activates Protein Kinase A (PKA).
- PKA phosphorylates **StAR protein**, facilitating cholesterol transport into the inner mitochondrial membrane for steroidogenesis.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: In the steroidogenic pathway, the enzyme [___] is responsible for the conversion of pregnenolone to progesterone.
back:
**3-beta-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase (3β-HSD)**

- Catalyzes the oxidation and isomerization of the B-ring.
- Essential step for producing both mineralocorticoids and sex steroids.
- Deficiency leads to ambiguous genitalia and salt wasting.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A patient presents with virilization and hypertension. Lab findings suggest a block in 11-beta-hydroxylase. Predict the effect on testosterone levels compared to 21-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency.
back:
**Increased Testosterone (Both Cases)**

- Both deficiencies block the cortisol pathway.
- Results in **increased ACTH**, stimulating the adrenal cortex.
- Accumulated precursors are shunted into the **androgen pathway**, causing hyperandrogenism and virilization.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Describe the biochemical role of Progesterone in maintaining the uterine environment during the luteal phase.
back:
**Secretory Transformation**

- Stimulates endometrial gland secretion and vascularization.
- Inhibits uterine contractions to allow implantation.
- Exerts **negative feedback** on the hypothalamus and pituitary to inhibit further LH/FSH surges.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Distinguish between the structural features of the A-ring in Testosterone versus Estradiol.
back:
**Aromatic vs. Non-Aromatic**

- **Estradiol:** Features a **phenolic/aromatic A-ring** (3 double bonds) with a C3 hydroxyl group.
- **Testosterone:** Features a non-aromatic ring with a **C3 keto group** and a C4-C5 double bond.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Identify the primary source of the 27-carbon precursor required for the synthesis of sex hormones in the gonads.
back:
**Plasma LDL and De Novo Synthesis**

- **Cholesterol** is the universal precursor.
- Primarily obtained from the uptake of **LDL particles** via receptor-mediated endocytosis.
- Can be synthesized de novo from **Acetyl-CoA** via the HMG-CoA reductase pathway.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: In the biosynthesis of all sex steroids, the transport of cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane is the rate-limiting control point mediated by the [___] protein.
back:
Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory (StAR) protein.
• Transports cholesterol to the inner mitochondrial membrane.
• Necessary for the activity of the side-chain cleavage enzyme.
• Activated via cAMP/PKA signaling.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A 60-year-old female with estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer is treated with a medication to block the conversion of androstenedione to estrone in adipose tissue. This drug targets the enzyme [___].
back:
Aromatase (CYP19).
• Catalyzes the conversion of androgens to estrogens.
• Found in ovaries and extragonadal sites (adipose, breast).
• Uses a Cytochrome P450 monooxygenase mechanism.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Detail the biochemical mechanism by which testosterone and estrogen interact with DNA to modulate gene expression.
back:
• Diffuse through plasma membranes and bind to nuclear receptors.
• Receptors undergo conformational change and dimerize.
• Complex binds to Hormone Response Elements (HREs) using zinc finger motifs.
• Recruits coactivators to initiate transcription.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the transport of sex steroids in the blood with the biochemical process required for their hepatic clearance.
back:
• Transport: Bound to Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG) or Albumin for systemic delivery.
• Clearance: Liver inactivates them via reduction of double bonds and conjugation with glucuronic acid or sulfate to increase water solubility for excretion.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Identify the pituitary hormone that stimulates the Corpus Luteum to secrete progesterone and the specific second messenger involved.
back:
• Hormone: Luteinizing Hormone (LH).
• Second Messenger: cAMP.
• Binding to GPCRs activates Adenylyl Cyclase, which elevates cAMP to stimulate progesterone synthesis.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: The initial enzymatic reaction in sex steroid synthesis converts cholesterol into the 21-carbon parent compound [___].
back:
Pregnenolone.
• Catalyzed by Cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme (Desmolase/P450scc).
• Requires NADPH and molecular oxygen.
• Occurs within the mitochondria.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A patient with severe liver failure develops feminization. Explain the biochemical role of the liver in maintaining normal male hormone balance that is failing here.
back:
• The liver performs catabolic conjugation of estrogens.
• Impaired liver function prevents the reduction and excretion of estrogens.
• Elevated estrogen-to-testosterone ratio leads to gynecomastia and other feminization symptoms.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Describe how the body ensures the coordinated regulation of multiple genes across different chromosomes in response to a single surge of testosterone.
back:
• Each responsive gene possesses an identical cis-acting Androgen Response Element (ARE).
• The trans-acting Testosterone-Receptor complex recognizes this specific sequence.
• Simultaneous binding to various HREs allows for the coordinate expression of the androgenic transcriptome.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Distinguish between the primary ovarian sources of Estrogen and Progesterone during the menstrual cycle.
back:
• Estrogen: Predominantly synthesized by the Granulosa cells of the developing follicle.
• Progesterone: Predominantly synthesized by the Corpus Luteum after ovulation.
• Both rely on the conversion of cholesterol via the Δ5 or Δ4 pathways.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Name the specific liver-synthesized protein that determines the bioavailability of testosterone by sequestering it in the plasma.
back:
Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG).
• High-affinity carrier for testosterone and estradiol.
• Only the 'free' (unbound) hormone is biologically active.
• Synthesis is increased by estrogen and decreased by androgens.

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: The rate-limiting step in the biosynthesis of all sex steroids involves the conversion of cholesterol to [___] by the enzyme P450scc (Desmolase).
back:
• Pregnenolone
• Occurs in the inner mitochondrial membrane
• Driven by LH in Leydig cells and FSH/LH in ovaries

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A 17-year-old male presents with delayed puberty and small testes. Labs show low testosterone but significantly elevated LH and FSH. This clinical pattern suggests [___].
back:
• Primary Hypogonadism
• Failure of Leydig/Sertoli cells (e.g., Klinefelter syndrome)
• Absence of negative feedback leads to pituitary over-secretion of gonadotropins

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Explain the 'Two-Cell, Two-Gonadotropin' mechanism of ovarian estrogen biosynthesis.
back:
• LH: Stimulates Theca cells to produce androstenedione from cholesterol
• FSH: Stimulates Granulosa cells to convert androstenedione to Estradiol
• Key Enzyme: Aromatase (CYP19)

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the physiological roles of Testosterone and its 5-alpha-reduced metabolite, Dihydrotestosterone (DHT).
back:
• Testosterone: Internal genitalia (Wolffian ducts), muscle mass, erythropoiesis
• DHT: External genitalia (penis/scrotum), prostate growth, male-pattern baldness
• DHT has higher affinity for the androgen receptor

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Identify the specific plasma protein that binds Testosterone and Estradiol with high affinity, and state the effect of liver cirrhosis on its levels.
back:
• Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG)
• Liver cirrhosis: Increases SHBG levels
• Result: Decreased free (active) testosterone, contributing to gynecomastia

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: During the follicular phase, sustained high levels of Estrogen switch from negative to positive feedback, resulting in the [___] surge.
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
• Occurs approximately 24-36 hours before ovulation
• Triggers rupture of the Graafian follicle

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: A woman in her first trimester of pregnancy presents with threatened abortion. Progesterone is administered to support the pregnancy because its biochemical role is to [___].
back:
• Maintain secretory endometrium for implantation
• Induce 'uterine quiescence' by inhibiting myometrial contractions
• Counteract the proliferative effects of estrogen

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Describe the intracellular path and mechanism of action for Estrogen from the plasma to gene induction.
back:
• Diffuses through membrane → Binds nuclear/cytosolic receptor
• Receptor dimerizes → Binds Estrogen Response Element (ERE) on DNA
• Uses Zinc Finger motifs to facilitate DNA binding and transcription

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Contrast the primary catabolic pathways and urinary excretion products of Progesterone versus Testosterone.
back:
• Progesterone: Reduced to Pregnanediol; excreted as glucuronide
• Testosterone: Converted to Androsterone/Etiocholanolone (17-ketosteroids)
• Both conjugated in the liver with glucuronic acid or sulfate

category: Explain the structure, biosynthesis, secretion, transport, regulation, catabolism, mechanism of action and biochemical role of testosterone, progesterone and estrogen
front: Explain why chronic use of exogenous anabolic steroids results in testicular atrophy.
back:
• High exogenous levels exert negative feedback on Hypothalamus/Pituitary
• Decreases GnRH, LH, and FSH secretion
• Loss of LH stimulation causes Leydig cell inactivity and atrophy

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: The primary mechanism of combined oral contraceptives involves the suppression of the mid-cycle [___] surge by providing negative feedback to the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
• Prevents ovulation by inhibiting the peak required for follicle rupture
• Maintains constant steroid levels to override the natural cycle.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A 28-year-old female takes a daily pill containing ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone. Explain the specific effect of the progestin component on her cervical mucus.
back:
• Increases viscosity and thickness
• Decreases amount of mucus
• Creates a physical barrier that prevents sperm penetration into the uterine cavity.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Describe the signal transduction sequence by which estrogen and progesterone regulate target gene expression in the reproductive tract.
back:
• Diffusion across plasma membrane
• Binding to intracellular (nuclear) receptors
• Dimerization and binding to DNA Hormone Response Elements (HREs)
• Recruitment of coactivators to alter mRNA transcription.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Contrast the physiological impact of exogenous estrogen on the endometrium versus the impact of synthetic progestins used in contraception.
back:
• Estrogen: Promotes endometrial proliferation and thickening
• Progestin: Induces secretory changes or endometrial atrophy
• Combined: Results in an environment unfavorable for blastocyst implantation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the enzymatic step targeted by aromatase inhibitors in the management of infertility related to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
back:
• Conversion of androgens (androstenedione/testosterone) to estrogens (estrone/estradiol)
• Inhibition reduces negative feedback on the hypothalamus
• Results in increased FSH secretion to stimulate follicular growth.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: In the management of anovulatory infertility, [___] acts as a selective estrogen receptor modulator that blocks hypothalamic estrogen receptors to increase GnRH pulse frequency.
back:
• Clomiphene citrate
• Interpreted by the brain as low estrogen levels
• Triggers compensatory rise in FSH and LH to induce ovulation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A patient presents with secondary infertility. Laboratory analysis reveals elevated prolactin, which is known to inhibit the pulsatile release of [___], thereby preventing the LH surge.
back:
• Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)
• Suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
• Leads to hypoestrogenism and anovulation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Explain why a genetic deficiency in the Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory (StAR) protein results in both adrenal failure and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.
back:
• StAR mediates cholesterol transport into mitochondria
• Essential for the rate-limiting step (P450scc activity)
• Prevents synthesis of all steroids (cortisol, aldosterone, and sex hormones).

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Distinguish between the negative and positive feedback loops of estrogen on the pituitary gland during a normal menstrual cycle.
back:
• Negative: Low/moderate estrogen inhibits FSH/LH (follicular phase)
• Positive: Sustained high estrogen (>200 pg/mL for 48h) triggers LH surge
• Contraceptives: Maintain negative feedback to prevent the positive switch.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Name the 21-carbon steroid precursor synthesized in the mitochondria that serves as the immediate parent compound for progesterone.
back:
• Pregnenolone
• Formed by side-chain cleavage of cholesterol
• Converted to progesterone by 3-β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: The large polypeptide precursor synthesized in the corticotrophs of the anterior pituitary that is proteolytically cleaved to yield ACTH, melanocyte-stimulating hormone, and endorphins is [___].
back:
• Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)
• It undergoes tissue-specific post-translational processing by prohormone convertases.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: A 40-year-old male with hypotension and fatigue exhibits a distinct bronze tint to his skin and palmar creases. Explain the biochemical link between his low cortisol levels and the hyperpigmentation.
back:
• Low cortisol removes negative feedback, increasing POMC synthesis.
• High ACTH levels (which share a common heptapeptide sequence with α-MSH) stimulate melanocyte receptors directly.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Describe the role of Prohormone Convertase 1 (PC1) in the synthesis and secretion of ACTH from the anterior pituitary.
back:
• PC1 cleaves the POMC precursor primarily into ACTH and β-lipotropin.
• These products are co-packaged into secretory granules for release.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Contrast the biological roles of ACTH versus β-endorphin, both of which are co-derived from the POMC gene product.
back:
• ACTH: Stimulates adrenal steroidogenesis (primarily cortisol).
• β-endorphin: Acts as an endogenous opioid to provide analgesia and modulate the stress response.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Name the specific steroid hormone that inhibits the transcription of the POMC gene and identify the primary organ where this regulation occurs.
back:
• Hormone: Cortisol.
• Organ: Anterior Pituitary (corticotrophs).

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
coreConcept: Structural Homology of ACTH and MSH
front: ACTH and MSH are structurally associated because ACTH contains the [___] sequence (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Arg-Trp-Gly), which allows it to activate melanocortin-1 receptors.
back:
• α-MSH core (Heptapeptide sequence)
• High concentrations of ACTH mimic MSH activity.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: A patient who underwent bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing's disease later develops an invasive pituitary tumor and intense hyperpigmentation. Identify this condition and the specific gene product being overexpressed.
back:
• Nelson Syndrome.
• Overexpression of the POMC gene (leading to excessive ACTH and MSH).

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Explain why MSH production is dominant in the intermediate lobe of the pituitary, whereas ACTH production is dominant in the anterior lobe.
back:
• Anterior Lobe: Contains PC1, which cleaves POMC into ACTH.
• Intermediate Lobe: Contains PC2, which further cleaves ACTH into α-MSH and CLIP.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Distinguish between the diagnostic significance of hyperpigmentation in primary versus secondary adrenal insufficiency.
back:
• Primary (Addison's): Hyperpigmentation is present due to high ACTH/POMC levels.
• Secondary (Pituitary failure): Hyperpigmentation is absent because ACTH levels are low.

category: Explain the synthesis and secretion of ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone) in association with melanocyte-stimulating hormone, lipotropin, and endorphin
front: Identify the hypothalamic peptide that stimulates the co-secretion of ACTH, β-lipotropin, and β-endorphin from pituitary secretory granules.
back:
• Corticotropin-Releasing Hormone (CRH).
• It initiates the signal for POMC cleavage and release during stress.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Combined oral contraceptives prevent pregnancy primarily by providing negative feedback to the hypothalamus and pituitary, which inhibits the secretion of [___].
back:
• GnRH, LH, and FSH.
• Prevents the mid-cycle LH surge.
• Effectively inhibits ovulation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A 26-year-old female presents with hirsutism, irregular periods, and infertility. Labs show an elevated LH:FSH ratio and increased androstenedione. Explain the biochemical basis of her infertility.
back:
• Disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis.
• High LH stimulates excess theca cell androgens.
• Peripheral conversion to estrogen inhibits FSH, preventing follicular maturation and ovulation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Describe the primary mechanisms by which progestin-only contraceptives prevent conception in addition to the partial inhibition of ovulation.
back:
• Thickening of cervical mucus to impede sperm penetration.
• Alteration of the endometrial lining to prevent implantation.
• Reduced ciliary activity in the fallopian tubes to slow ovum transport.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Contrast the effects of combined oral contraceptives versus progestin-only pills on the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis.
back:
• Combined: Consistently suppress FSH and LH to block ovulation.
• Progestin-only: Inconsistently inhibit ovulation (approx. 60-80%).
• Progestin-only relies more heavily on peripheral effects like cervical mucus changes.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Explain why aromatase inhibitors like letrozole are used as ovulation induction agents in women with infertility.
back:
• Block conversion of androgens to estrogens.
• Decreased estrogen levels reduce negative feedback to the pituitary.
• Triggers increased FSH secretion to stimulate follicle development.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Steroid hormones used in contraception exert their effects by binding to intracellular receptors that interact with specific DNA sequences called [___].
back:
• Hormone Response Elements (HREs).
• These utilize zinc finger motifs for DNA binding.
• Modulate transcription of targeted genes in reproductive tissues.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A patient with infertility is prescribed Clomiphene citrate. Describe the biochemical mechanism by which this drug promotes follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) release.
back:
• Acts as a Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM).
• Blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus.
• Inhibits estrogen's negative feedback, increasing GnRH and FSH pulse frequency.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Detail the role of progesterone in preparing the endometrium for potential pregnancy during the luteal phase.
back:
• Induces secretory transformation of the endometrium.
• Increases vascularity and gland complexity.
• Downregulates estrogen receptors to facilitate a receptive environment for blastocyst implantation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Distinguish between natural estradiol and the ethinyl estradiol used in oral contraceptives regarding hepatic metabolism.
back:
• Natural estradiol: Subject to rapid first-pass metabolism.
• Ethinyl estradiol: Contains an ethinyl group at C17.
• Prevents hepatic oxidation, significantly increasing oral bioavailability and half-life.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Name the 27-carbon precursor required for the synthesis of both progestins and estrogens, and state the cellular location of its initial cleavage.
back:
• Cholesterol is the precursor.
• Initial side-chain cleavage occurs in the mitochondria.
• Catalyzed by the enzyme P450scc (desmolase) to produce pregnenolone.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Steroid hormones, such as those found in oral contraceptives, are lipophilic and typically exert their biological effects by binding to [___] inside the target cell.
back:
• Intracellular/Nuclear receptors
  • Function as ligand-activated transcription factors
  • Regulate gene expression via Hormone Response Elements (HREs)

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A 24-year-old female takes a combined oral contraceptive pill. This medication prevents pregnancy primarily by exerting negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary to suppress the mid-cycle surge of [___].
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
  • Inhibition of the LH surge prevents ovulation
  • Also suppresses FSH to inhibit follicular development

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Explain the biochemical role of the estrogen component in oral contraceptives regarding the selection of the dominant follicle.
back:
• Suppresses FSH secretion from the anterior pituitary
  • Prevents the development and maturation of a dominant follicle
  • Provides negative feedback to the hypothalamic-pituitary axis

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Contrast the primary contraceptive mechanism of progestins with that of estrogens in combined hormonal therapy.
back:
• Progestins: Thickens cervical mucus (blocks sperm) and inhibits LH surge
  • Estrogens: Primarily suppresses FSH (prevents follicular maturation)
  • Progestins also alter endometrium to inhibit implantation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the synthesis of all steroid hormones from cholesterol.
back:
• Desmolase (P450scc / Side-chain cleavage enzyme)
  • Converts Cholesterol to Pregnenolone
  • Activated by LH in the gonads and ACTH in the adrenals

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: In the hormonal management of infertility, the secondary messenger system utilized by the FSH and LH receptors in the ovary is [___].
back:
• Cyclic AMP (cAMP) pathway
  • Involves Gs-protein activation of Adenylyl Cyclase
  • Leads to Protein Kinase A (PKA) activation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A woman presenting with primary infertility has very high serum FSH and LH levels but negligible estradiol. This hormonal profile indicates a defect located at the [___].
back:
• Ovaries (Primary Hypogonadism)
  • Indicates ovarian failure or resistance
  • Loss of negative feedback leads to pituitary overproduction of gonadotropins

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Describe the mechanism by which high-dose progestins are used in 'minipills' or emergency contraception to prevent pregnancy after intercourse.
back:
• Inhibit or delay ovulation by blunting the LH surge
  • Increase cervical mucus viscosity to prevent sperm penetration
  • May alter endometrial receptivity for implantation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Distinguish the metabolic fate of the steroid-receptor complex after dimerization has occurred in the nucleus.
back:
• Binds to specific DNA sequences (Hormone Response Elements)
  • Utilizes Zinc Finger motifs to interact with major grooves
  • Recruits coactivators/corepressors to modulate mRNA transcription

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Specify the essential 21-carbon steroid precursor formed immediately after side-chain cleavage of cholesterol.
back:
• Pregnenolone
  • Parent compound for all steroid classes (progestins, estrogens, androgens)
  • Synthesized in the inner mitochondrial membrane

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: During steroidogenesis, the rate-limiting enzyme that converts cholesterol into pregnenolone within the mitochondria is [___].
back:
• P450scc (Cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme)
  • Also known as Desmolase
  • Requires NADPH and O2
  • Located on the inner mitochondrial membrane

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
coreConcept: Mechanism of Action of Combined OCPs
front: A 24-year-old female is prescribed a combined oral contraceptive pill. This medication prevents pregnancy primarily by providing negative feedback to suppress the mid-cycle surge of which pituitary hormone?
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
  • Suppression of the LH surge prevents ovulation
  • Also suppresses FSH to inhibit follicle maturation
  • Secondary effects include thickening of cervical mucus

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Describe the sequence of events after a lipophilic steroid hormone (e.g., Estrogen) enters the nucleus of a target cell to influence fertility.
back:
• Hormone binds to specific nuclear receptor
  • Receptor-ligand complex dimerizes
  • Complex binds to DNA at Hormone Response Elements (HREs)
  • Recruits coactivators/corepressors to regulate gene transcription

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Contrast the specific physiologic roles of the Estrogenic versus Progestogenic components in pharmacological contraception.
back:
• Estrogen: Primarily suppresses FSH, preventing the selection and emergence of a dominant follicle
  • Progestogen: Primarily suppresses LH surge (inhibiting ovulation) and renders cervical mucus hostile to sperm

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the protein that facilitates the essential, rate-limiting transport of cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane.
back:
• Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory (StAR) protein
  • Crucial control point for all steroid hormone synthesis
  • Activated by PKA-mediated phosphorylation in response to ACTH/LH

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: The DNA-binding domain of steroid hormone receptors contains a structural motif used to recognize specific HRE sequences known as a [___].
back:
• Zinc finger
  • Uses zinc ions to stabilize protein folds
  • Allows the receptor to act as a ligand-activated transcription factor

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A female patient with ambiguous genitalia and primary infertility is found to have a 21-α-hydroxylase deficiency. Explain the biochemical cause of her virilization.
back:
• Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH)
  • Reduced cortisol leads to increased ACTH
  • Steroid precursors are shunted into the androgen synthesis pathway
  • Excess androgens cause virilization and HPG axis disruption

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Explain the biochemical rationale for using GnRH agonists in a continuous (non-pulsatile) fashion to treat infertility associated with endometriosis.
back:
• Continuous administration causes downregulation of pituitary GnRH receptors
  • Results in 'medical oophorectomy' (hypogonadotropic state)
  • Decreases estrogen production
  • Suppresses growth of ectopic endometrial tissue

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Distinguish the cellular location and receptor characteristics of steroid hormones compared to peptide hormones like Glucagon.
back:
• Steroids: Intracellular/Nuclear receptors; act via gene transcription (slow response)
  • Glucagon: Plasma membrane GPCR; acts via second messengers like cAMP (rapid response)

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Name the specific steroid hormone produced by the corpus luteum that is vital for maintaining the secretory endometrium and preventing early pregnancy loss.
back:
• Progesterone
  • Prepares endometrium for implantation
  • Exerts negative feedback on LH/FSH during the luteal phase
  • Deficiency can lead to luteal phase defect and infertility

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
coreConcept: Mechanism of LH suppression in OCPs
front: Combined oral contraceptives provide negative feedback to the anterior pituitary, primarily suppressing the mid-cycle surge of [___] to prevent ovulation.
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
• Prevents the trigger for follicular rupture
• Results in anovulatory cycles

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A 26-year-old female starting a combined oral contraceptive (COC) asks how the estrogen component helps prevent pregnancy. At the biochemical level, estrogen primarily inhibits the release of [___].
back:
• Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
• Suppresses early follicular development
• Prevents the selection of a dominant follicle

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: How do progestins in oral contraceptives alter the female reproductive tract environment to impede fertilization and implantation?
back:
• Thicken cervical mucus to block sperm migration
• Induce endometrial atrophy
• Create an environment unreceptive to blastocyst implantation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A woman on a 'Mini-pill' (progestin-only) misses a dose and becomes pregnant, whereas women on combined pills have higher efficacy. Contrast the primary mechanisms of these two contraceptive types.
back:
• Combined pills: Consistently inhibit ovulation via FSH/LH suppression
• Progestin-only: Primarily rely on cervical mucus thickening; may not always suppress ovulation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the hypothalamic signaling molecule whose pulsatile secretion is decreased by the chronic administration of exogenous steroid contraceptives.
back:
• Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)
• Leads to downstream reduction in FSH and LH
• Essential for pharmacological contraception

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: In pharmacological management of anovulatory infertility, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is utilized as a surrogate for [___] to induce final oocyte maturation.
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
• Binds to the same LHCG receptor
• Triggers ovulation in stimulated follicles

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A patient with infertility due to PCOS is treated with Clomiphene citrate. Explain the biochemical mechanism by which this drug stimulates ovulation.
back:
• Blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus
• Inhibits negative feedback by endogenous estrogen
• Increases GnRH pulse frequency and FSH/LH secretion

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A woman with recurrent early pregnancy loss is diagnosed with Luteal Phase Deficiency. Explain the mechanism of steroid hormone therapy used in this case.
back:
• Progesterone supplementation provides secretory transformation of endometrium
• Supports early decidualization
• Maintains the pregnancy until placental shift

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Distinguish between the hormonal profiles of infertility caused by Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) versus Primary Ovarian Insufficiency (POI) regarding gonadotropins.
back:
• PCOS: High LH-to-FSH ratio; dysfunctional feedback
• POI: Elevated FSH and LH due to lack of estrogenic negative feedback (ovarian failure)

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Which steroid hormone is measured in the mid-luteal phase to biochemically confirm that ovulation has occurred in an infertile patient?
back:
• Progesterone
• Produced by the corpus luteum
• Levels >3 ng/mL generally indicate successful ovulation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: In the biosynthesis of all steroid hormones, the rate-limiting step involves the conversion of cholesterol to [___] by the mitochondrial enzyme desmolase (P450scc).
back:
• Pregnenolone.
• Requires NADPH and molecular oxygen.
• Occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
• Mediated by StAR protein transport.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A 26-year-old female on combined oral contraceptive pills (estrogen and progestin) fails to ovulate. This pharmacological effect is achieved by suppressing the mid-cycle surge of [___].
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH).
• Estrogen/progestin provide negative feedback to the hypothalamus and pituitary.
• Inhibits GnRH pulsatility and FSH/LH release.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Explain how the progestin component of oral contraceptives contributes to infertility/contraception beyond the inhibition of ovulation.
back:
• Thickens cervical mucus to impede sperm penetration.
• Induces endometrial atrophy to prevent implantation.
• Decreases fallopian tube motility.
• Blunts the LH response to estrogen.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A woman presenting with primary infertility has high serum FSH and LH but very low estradiol. Contrast this with the findings expected in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
back:
• Primary Failure: High FSH/LH due to lack of negative feedback (ovarian defect).
• Hypogonadotropic: Low FSH/LH and low estradiol (pituitary/hypothalamic defect).

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Describe the specific structural motif used by the estrogen-receptor complex to interact with DNA at the Hormone Response Element (HRE).
back:
• Zinc finger motif.
• Coordinates a zinc ion with cysteine/histidine residues.
• Allows the receptor to bind the major groove of DNA.
• Initiates gene transcription.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A common biochemical feature of infertility associated with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is an abnormally elevated ratio of [___] to [___].
back:
• LH to FSH ratio (often >2:1 or 3:1).
• High LH stimulates excess ovarian androgen production.
• Low FSH prevents proper follicular maturation and ovulation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A patient is prescribed Clomiphene citrate to treat infertility. Explain the biochemical mechanism by which this drug induces ovulation.
back:
• Estrogen receptor antagonist in the hypothalamus.
• Blocks negative feedback of endogenous estrogen.
• Increases GnRH frequency and FSH/LH secretion.
• Stimulates multiple follicular development.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Distinguish between the roles of the two distinct cell types in the 'Two-Cell, Two-Gonadotropin' model of ovarian estrogen synthesis.
back:
• Theca Cells: LH stimulates androgen synthesis from cholesterol.
• Granulosa Cells: FSH stimulates Aromatase to convert theca-derived androgens into estradiol.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Contrast the feedback effects of estrogen on LH secretion during the early follicular phase versus the late follicular phase.
back:
• Early/Mid Phase: Low estrogen levels exert negative feedback on LH.
• Late Phase: Sustained high estrogen levels (>200 pg/mL) exert positive feedback, triggering the LH surge.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the specific hepatic-derived glycoprotein responsible for the high-affinity transport of estradiol and testosterone in the plasma.
back:
• Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG).
• Only the 'free' (unbound) steroid is biologically active.
• SHBG levels are increased by estrogen and decreased by androgens.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: The parent compound for all steroid hormones, synthesized from cholesterol within the inner mitochondrial membrane, is [___].
back:
• Pregnenolone.
• Derived via side-chain cleavage of cholesterol.
• Serves as the precursor for progestins, androgens, and estrogens.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A 26-year-old female on combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs) remains non-ovulatory. This therapeutic effect is achieved by preventing the mid-cycle surge of which hormone?
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH).
• COCPs provide negative feedback to the pituitary.
• Suppression of the LH surge directly inhibits ovulation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Describe the molecular sequence of events after a steroid hormone binds to its intracellular receptor.
back:
• Receptor-ligand complex dimerizes.
• Complex translocates to the nucleus.
• Binds to DNA at Hormone Response Elements (HREs).
• Recruits coactivators/corepressors to regulate gene transcription.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Contrast the primary roles of FSH and LH in the context of male and female infertility.
back:
• FSH: Stimulates follicular growth (females) and spermatogenesis (males).
• LH: Triggers ovulation/progesterone production (females) and testosterone synthesis in Leydig cells (males).

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the specific protein required to transport cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane during steroidogenesis.
back:
• Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory (StAR) protein.
• It is a critical control point for hormone synthesis.
• Facilitates access to the cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: In the mechanism of oral contraception, the synthetic progestin component primarily prevents pregnancy by [___].
back:
• Thickening cervical mucus to block sperm entry.
• Inhibiting the LH surge to prevent ovulation.
• Altering the endometrium to discourage implantation.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A patient presents with infertility and is found to have a deficiency in the side-chain cleavage enzyme (desmolase). What is the biochemical consequence for steroid production?
back:
• Global deficiency in all steroid hormone classes.
• Inability to convert cholesterol to pregnenolone.
• Results in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) and reproductive failure.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Explain how the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis is manipulated by exogenous steroids to induce infertility.
back:
• Synthetic estrogens/progestins exert constant negative feedback.
• Suppresses Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus.
• Decreases pituitary FSH and LH, halting the ovarian cycle.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Contrast the physical location and general response time of steroid hormone receptors with those of peptide hormones like Glucagon.
back:
• Steroid Receptors: Intracellular (cytosolic or nuclear); slow response (hours/days) via transcription.
• Peptide Receptors: Plasma membrane-bound; rapid response (seconds/minutes) via second messenger cascades.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the mitochondrial enzyme that acts as the rate-limiting catalyst for all steroid hormone biosynthesis.
back:
• P450scc (also called Desmolase or Side-Chain Cleavage Enzyme).
• Requires NADPH and molecular oxygen.
• Converts C27 cholesterol into C21 pregnenolone.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs) primarily prevent pregnancy by inhibiting the mid-cycle surge of [___] from the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
• High exogenous steroid levels provide negative feedback
• Inhibition of this surge directly prevents ovulation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A 28-year-old female taking a progesterone-only "mini-pill" asks how it works if she still occasionally ovulates. Explain the non-ovulatory contraceptive mechanism.
back:
• Thickens cervical mucus to impede sperm penetration
• Induces endometrial changes that inhibit implantation
• Reduces fallopian tube ciliary motility

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Describe how exogenous estrogen in oral contraceptives contributes to the prevention of follicular maturation.
back:
• Suppresses Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
• Acts via negative feedback on the pituitary
• Prevents selection and growth of a dominant follicle

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
coreConcept: Steroid Hormones in Contraception vs Infertility
front: Contrast the feedback effects of steroid-based contraception on the HPO axis with its role in treating luteal phase defects in infertility.
back:
• Contraception: Constant steroid levels provide negative feedback to block the LH surge.
• Infertility: Progesterone provides luteal support by preparing a receptive secretory endometrium.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Identify the steroid-related biochemical cause of infertility often managed with aromatase inhibitors or clomiphene citrate.
back:
• Estrogen-mediated negative feedback suppression of GnRH/FSH
• Drugs block estrogen receptors or synthesis
• Disinhibits the pituitary to stimulate ovulation

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: In the treatment of female infertility, [___] is often administered during the second half of the menstrual cycle to support potential embryo implantation.
back:
• Progesterone
• Essential for maintaining the decidua
• Supports the secretory phase of the endometrium

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: A patient with PCOS and infertility is treated with an agent that blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus. Explain the resulting change in FSH levels.
back:
• FSH levels increase
• Hypothalamus perceives low estrogen and increases GnRH
• Pituitary responds by secreting more FSH to recruit follicles

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which steroid hormones in contraceptives alter gene expression in target endometrial cells.
back:
• Bind to intracellular or nuclear receptors
• Receptor-hormone complex binds to DNA Hormone Response Elements (HRE)
• Acts as a transcription factor to modulate mRNA synthesis

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Distinguish between the primary contraceptive roles of synthetic estrogens and progestins in combined formulations.
back:
• Estrogens: Primarily suppress FSH to prevent follicle selection.
• Progestins: Primarily suppress LH to prevent ovulation and thicken mucus.

category: Discuss the role of steroid hormones in oral contraception, Infertility
front: Name the specific cholesterol-derived precursor required for the synthesis of all reproductive steroid hormones used in infertility management.
back:
• Pregnenolone
• Formed by the side-chain cleavage enzyme (P450scc)
• Initial rate-limiting step in steroidogenesis

category: Define the following terms: chromosome, allele (dominant and recessive), gene, locus, heterozygote, homozygote, hemizygous, autosome, genotype, phenotype, haploid and diploid number of chromosomes, aneuploidy, proband, proposita, pedigree, propositus, penetrance, codominance and polygenic
front: The specific physical location or position of a gene on a chromosome is known as its [___].
back:
* Locus
* Represents the gene's 'address'
* Essential for mapping and identifying genetic linkages.

category: Define the following terms: chromosome, allele (dominant and recessive), gene, locus, heterozygote, homozygote, hemizygous, autosome, genotype, phenotype, haploid and diploid number of chromosomes, aneuploidy, proband, proposita, pedigree, propositus, penetrance, codominance and polygenic
front: A 10-year-old male with Hemophilia A is the first individual in his family to be clinically identified and brought to a geneticist's attention. This index case is referred to as the [___].
back:
* Proband (or Propositus)
* Proposita refers to a female index case
* Represented by an arrow in pedigree charts to signify the clinical starting point.

category: Define the following terms: chromosome, allele (dominant and recessive), gene, locus, heterozygote, homozygote, hemizygous, autosome, genotype, phenotype, haploid and diploid number of chromosomes, aneuploidy, proband, proposita, pedigree, propositus, penetrance, codominance and polygenic
front: Explain the mechanism of 'incomplete penetrance' as observed in certain autosomal dominant disorders.
back:
* Proportion of individuals with a genotype who actually express the phenotype
* Results in individuals carrying the mutant allele but showing zero clinical signs
* Influenced by environmental and modifier gene interactions.

category: Define the following terms: chromosome, allele (dominant and recessive), gene, locus, heterozygote, homozygote, hemizygous, autosome, genotype, phenotype, haploid and diploid number of chromosomes, aneuploidy, proband, proposita, pedigree, propositus, penetrance, codominance and polygenic
front: Contrast the inheritance pattern of the AB blood group with that of skin color or height.
back:
* AB Blood: Codominance (both alleles A and B are fully and equally expressed)
* Skin/Height: Polygenic (trait controlled by multiple independent genes)
* Polygenic inheritance creates a continuous spectrum of phenotypes.

category: Define the following terms: chromosome, allele (dominant and recessive), gene, locus, heterozygote, homozygote, hemizygous, autosome, genotype, phenotype, haploid and diploid number of chromosomes, aneuploidy, proband, proposita, pedigree, propositus, penetrance, codominance and polygenic
front: Define the term 'hemizygous' in the context of X-linked genes in human males.
back:
* Possession of only one copy of a specific gene
* Occurs in males (XY) for all genes on the X and Y chromosomes
* Explains high prevalence of X-linked recessive traits in males.

category: Define the following terms: chromosome, allele (dominant and recessive), gene, locus, heterozygote, homozygote, hemizygous, autosome, genotype, phenotype, haploid and diploid number of chromosomes, aneuploidy, proband, proposita, pedigree, propositus, penetrance, codominance and polygenic
front: An abnormality in the number of chromosomes involving the loss or gain of a single chromosome (e.g., Trisomy 21) is technically defined as [___].
back:
* Aneuploidy
* Result of non-disjunction during meiosis
* Distinct from polyploidy, which involves entire extra sets of chromosomes.
